original_value: Land cover information plays an important role in mapping ecological and environmental changes in Earth’s diverse landscapes for ecosystem monitoring. Remote sensing data have been widely used for the study of land cover, enabling efficient mapping of changes of the Earth surface from Space. Although the availability of high-resolution remote sensing imagery increases significantly every year, traditional land cover analysis approaches based on pixel and object levels are not optimal. Recent advancement in deep learning has achieved remarkable success on image recognition field and has shown potential in high spatial resolution remote sensing applications, including classification and object detection. In this paper, a comprehensive review on land cover classification and object detection approaches using high resolution imagery is provided. Through two case studies, we demonstrated the applications of the state-of-the-art deep learning models to high spatial resolution remote sensing data for land cover classification and object detection and evaluated their performances against traditional approaches. For a land cover classification task, the deep-learning-based methods provide an end-to-end solution by using both spatial and spectral information. They have shown better performance than the traditional pixel-based method, especially for the categories of different vegetation. For an objective detection task, the deep-learning-based object detection method achieved more than 98% accuracy in a large area; its high accuracy and efficiency could relieve the burden of the traditional, labour-intensive method. However, considering the diversity of remote sensing data, more training datasets are required in order to improve the generalisation and the robustness of deep learning-based models.

result.paraphrase: Land-cover information is essential for mapping ecological and environmental changes across Earth’s varied landscapes and for ecosystem monitoring. Remote sensing data have been widely used in land-cover studies, allowing efficient mapping of changes to the Earth’s surface from space. Although high-resolution remote sensing imagery has become increasingly available each year, conventional land-cover analysis methods based on pixels and objects are not ideal. Recent advances in deep learning have produced impressive results in image recognition and shown promise for high-spatial-resolution remote sensing applications, including classification and object detection. This paper presents a comprehensive review of land-cover classification and object-detection methods using high-resolution imagery. Through two case studies, we demonstrated how state-of-the-art deep learning models can be applied to high-spatial-resolution remote sensing data for land-cover classification and object detection, and assessed their performance against traditional approaches. For land-cover classification, deep-learning-based methods offer an end-to-end solution by using both spatial and spectral information. They have outperformed the traditional pixel-based method, particularly for categories involving different vegetation. For object detection, the deep-learning-based method achieved over 98% accuracy over a large area; its accuracy and efficiency could reduce the burden of the traditional labor-intensive approach. However, given the diversity of remote sensing data, more training datasets are needed to improve the generalization and robustness of deep learning-based models.
